name: Paraiba Tourmaline
spiritual: Brings a sense of spiritual freshness
physical: Traditionally associated with a cooling, refreshing sense of calm
Said to ease stress held in the throat and neck
Crystal healers link it with a feeling of renewal
summary: Paraiba Tourmaline glows electric turquoise-blue from copper, one of the rarest gems on Earth, linked with heartfelt speech, calm and renewal.
intro: Paraiba tourmaline is the neon star of the gem trade. Its colour, an electric turquoise, aqua or violet-blue that seems lit from within, is created by traces of copper and manganese, a combination almost unknown in other tourmalines. Crystals are tiny by comparison with most gems, so a clean stone over a few carats is a major rarity. The gem looks like a swimming pool in sunlight or a tropical lagoon, and nothing else quite matches the vivid, saturated hue. Collectors hold it in extraordinary esteem, and an entire gem category is built around the name, though few crystal fans will ever own a faceted example.
history: Paraiba tourmaline was discovered in 1987 by Heitor Dimas Barbosa, a Brazilian prospector who spent years digging in a hill near the town of Sao Jose da Batalha in Paraiba state, convinced that something remarkable lay below. His persistence paid off when the first neon-blue crystals came to light, sparking a gem rush. The colour was a mystery until copper was identified as the chromophore, a first for tourmaline. When the Brazilian deposits became depleted, similar copper-bearing tourmaline was found in Nigeria and Mozambique. The trade still debates whether non-Brazilian stones may carry the Paraiba name, and laboratories issue origin reports to settle it.
meaning: In the crystal tradition Paraiba tourmaline is regarded as a stone of refreshment and heartfelt expression. Its colour sits between the throat and heart chakras, so practitioners link it with speaking from the heart and feeling at ease while doing so. Many people regard it as a talisman for creative renewal, for letting go of old stories and beginning with clear water. Because of its rarity, it is also seen as a stone for appreciating what is precious and unique within oneself. Healers say it brings a sense of calm similar to standing beside a still tropical sea. Physically it is traditionally associated with a feeling of freshness and relief from stress, a gentle support rather than a treatment.
howToUse: Most people will meet Paraiba as a pendant or ring, so wear it when you want to feel bright, calm and articulate. If you have a raw specimen or small tumbled piece, hold it during meditation and imagine clear turquoise light flowing through the throat and chest. Place a sample on a desk to encourage open, honest conversation, or beside your bed to wind down. For budget alternatives, many crystal fans substitute blue apatite, larimar or indicolite for similar energy work.
care: Paraiba tourmaline is hard and generally stable, so a gentle wash in lukewarm water with mild soap is fine, and it also responds to smoke, sound or moonlight cleansing. Avoid ultrasonic and steam cleaners, because many stones are heated and fracture-filled stones may be affected. Sunlight is not usually a problem, but extended heat should be avoided. Store each stone separately in a soft pouch and keep it away from harder gems that could scratch the surface.
identify: True Paraiba tourmaline is identified by its copper-bearing chemistry, which only a gemological laboratory can confirm, and its trademark neon colour that appears to glow. Imitations include apatite, blue topaz, fluorite, synthetic spinel and dyed or doped glass. Heat treatment is standard and accepted if disclosed. Because prices can reach thousands per carat, always buy with a certificate from a reputable lab that states the species, copper content, origin where possible and any treatments.

faq.q: Why is Paraiba tourmaline so expensive?
faq.a: Its neon colour is caused by copper, an unusual cause in tourmaline, and the deposits were small and are mostly worked out. Clean crystals are tiny, so demand far exceeds supply, driving prices very high.

faq.q: What is Paraiba tourmaline used for?
faq.a: In crystal tradition, it is used for heartfelt communication, calm and a sense of renewal. It is linked with the throat and heart chakras and valued as a rare, special talisman.
Yes. Blue apatite, larimar, indicolite and blue topaz offer similar sea-blue colours and are often used in crystal practice for comparable calm and communication themes at a much lower cost.
